validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/STATUS/SPEC confirmed at high confidence, not a GEM-only entity. Great Lakes Gas Transmission Limited Partnership is a real, active, FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas pipeline: it filed a prior-notice request with FERC on 2026-03-06 (Docket CP26-138-000, published Federal Register 91 FR 13306, 2026-03-19) to restore MAOP on its '36-inch-diameter Mainlines 100, 200, and 300' between the Shevlin and Deer River compressor stations in Minnesota -- an active 2026 regulatory filing is about as strong an existence signal as this project gets. Separately, FERC's 2014 prior-notice docket (2014-08053) and a 2022 abandonment application (referenced in FERC Docket, filed 2022-12-19) confirm the same entity, at 717/700 Louisiana/Texas St, Houston TX, continuously active across at least 2014-2026. A Michigan state regulator (EGLE) on-site inspection of Compressor Station #7 (Wakefield, MI, SRN N2168, activity date 2022-05-26) independently confirms: 2,115 miles, ~2,400 MMcf/d average design capacity, in business since 1967, 14 compressor stations (5 in the UP), owned by TransCanada/TC Energy -- a state environmental regulator inspecting a physical facility is a wholly independent origin from FERC or the operator's own site. TC Energy's own operations page and Wikipedia both restate the same 2,115-mi/3,404-km, 1967, Emerson MB-to-Minnesota/Wisconsin/Michigan/Eastern Canada description. Status=operating, Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission all confirmed by this pool -- an interstate FERC Sec. 7 pipeline actively filing rate/pressure dockets in 2026 is unambiguously an operating gas transmission line, not gathering/distribution. No duplicate risk: no other roster row is named Great Lakes or plausibly the same physical line (Viking, the other MB/MN-Canada crossing on this roster, is a separate TC Energy-affiliated system through a different corridor -- see cross_row_leads). Opened all 5 harvested wiki-pool citations: the Wikipedia mirror (via the bit.ly redirect) and the TC Energy operations page are live and usable; the SEC 10-K (TC PipeLines LP FY2011 annual report) is live (200) once fetched with an SEC-compliant User-Agent (SEC returns 403 to the default UA) and is a genuinely independent, pre-2021-merger SEC filing; the tcpipelineslp.com/assets/great-lakes/ URL now 302-redirects to tcenergy.com's homepage (the old TC PipeLines LP microsite is retired, consistent with the entity going private in 2021 -- not a value change, just a dead link, not swapped for anything since it carried no unique value); the 2007 Natural Gas Intelligence article URL likewise now redirects to NGI's current homepage nav with no article content -- both are dead/redirected pool citations that added nothing new, noted here for completeness rather than cited.

validity.researcher_notes: Tested the batch brief's lead that 'TC PipeLines LP is a dissolved entity' -- this does NOT hold for Great Lakes' ownership row, and the sheet's current Owner1/Owner2 values are correct, not stale. TC Energy completed a merger absorbing TC PipeLines LP's publicly-held common units on 2021-03-03 (TC Energy press release 'TC Energy and TC PipeLines, LP complete merger'; TCP Form 425/8-K filings on SEC EDGAR, Dec 2020-Mar 2021), which made TCP an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of TC Energy and delisted its units -- but this dissolved TCP's status as a PUBLIC MLP, not the LP entity itself. TC PipeLines LP continued to exist post-merger and continued holding its 46.45% interest in Great Lakes: its own consolidated financial statements for FY2024 (published on tcenergy.com, 'TC Pipelines, LP Consolidated Financial Statements December 31, 2024 and 2023') report equity-method goodwill tied to the Great Lakes investment unchanged at $39 million across both 2023 and 2024. TC Energy's own Great Lakes operator page (tcplus.com/Great%20Lakes, the regulatory/EBB site, not the marketing site) states in the present tense: 'TC PipeLines, LP owns 46.45 percent of Great Lakes. The remaining 53.55 percent is held by subsidiaries of TC Energy' -- matching GEM's Owner1(TC Energy 53.55%)/Owner2(TC PipeLines LP 46.45%) exactly. A second, fully independent origin -- TC PipeLines LP's own FY2011 SEC 10-K annual report (filed a decade before the 2021 merger) -- states the identical 46.45%/53.55% split, meaning this ownership structure has been stable for 15+ years and long predates the entity going private. So: GEM's values are current and correct; the only caveat worth a ResearcherNotes line is that 'TC PipeLines LP' is now a private subsidiary rather than a public company, which does not change the ownership percentages recorded here.

validity.researcher_notes: Geography defect flagged in the batch brief, confirmed. Every independent source consulted describes ONE physical terminus for the mainline: 'extending from the Canadian border near Emerson, Manitoba, Canada to St. Clair, Michigan, near Detroit' (TC PipeLines LP FY2011 SEC 10-K, verbatim); 'opened in 1967, running 2,115 miles... between Emerson, Manitoba and St. Clair, Michigan' (Wikipedia); the Michigan state regulator's inspection report likewise places GLGT's Michigan compressor stations (including the Upper Peninsula cluster and Station #7 near Wakefield) along a route terminating in Michigan, not in Wisconsin, Minnesota, or 'Eastern Canada'. The current EndState/Province value, 'Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Eastern Canada,' is TC Energy's own marketing-page description of the MARKETS the pipeline serves along its corridor ('the most direct... link between Western Canada's natural gas basins and population centers in Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan and Eastern Canada') -- not a list of endpoints, and it has been copied into a single-terminus field. TC Energy's own operator/regulatory site (tcplus.com) separately lists 'Terminates Near: Sault Ste. Marie, ON, Canada and St. Clair, MI' -- Sault Ste. Marie appears to be where GLGT interconnects into TransCanada's Mainline system serving Ontario/Dawn, not a second GLGT terminus; every other independent source (SEC 10-K, Wikipedia, EGLE) states the terminus as St. Clair, MI alone, so I am proposing Michigan (not a compound value) as the sourced EndState/Province. StartState/Province is simply blank despite StartPrefecture/District already correctly holding 'Manitoba' -- filling it is a mechanical completion, not new research.

cross_row_leads.facts: TC PipeLines LP's FY2011 10-K: 'The Northern Border pipeline system consists of 1,407 miles of pipeline extending from the Canadian border near Port of Morgan, Montana, to a terminus near North Hayden, Indiana, south of Chicago. Northern Border has an average design capacity of approximately 2.4 Bcf/d [2,400 MMcf/d] at Port of Morgan, Montana. Construction... initially completed in 1982.' Roster shows P2099 len=1412.0 (vs 1,407 here -- close but not exact, worth a length check) and cap=2400.00 (exact match).

Same 10-K: 'The GTN pipeline system consists of 1,353 miles of pipeline extending from an interconnection near Kingsgate, British Columbia, Canada at the Canadian border to a point near Malin, Oregon at the California border. The GTN pipeline has an average design capacity of approximately 2.9 Bcf/d [2,900 MMcf/d] at Kingsgate. The original construction... was completed in 1961.' Matches roster P0231 exactly (len=1353.0, cap=2900.00) -- a clean confirmation source if GTN hasn't already been sourced.

Same 10-K: 'The Bison pipeline system consists of 303 miles of pipeline extending from the Powder River Basin near Gillette, Wyoming to Northern Border's pipeline system in Morton County, North Dakota. The Bison pipeline system was placed into service in January 2011 and has an average design capacity without compression of 407 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d).' Roster shows P0158 len=302.0 (close match) but cap=477.00 -- a materially different capacity from this 2011 figure. Could be a post-2011 compression addition (the 10-K caveats 'without compression'), but worth checking whoever sources P0158's Capacity cell against this 407 MMcf/d 2011 baseline.

Same 10-K: 'The North Baja pipeline system consists of 86 miles of pipeline extending from an interconnection with the El Paso Natural Gas Company (EPNG) pipeline near Ehrenberg, Arizona, to an interconnection with the Gasoducto Rosarito natural gas pipeline near Ogilby, California on the Mexican border... an average design capacity of 500 MMcf/d for southbound transportation and 600 MMcf/d for northbound transportation. The North Baja pipeline system was initially placed into service in 2002, followed by expansions and extensions in 2008 and 2010.' Roster shows P0226 cap=600.00 (matches northbound figure exactly) but len=129.0 vs this 86-mile 2011 figure -- the gap is plausibly a later post-2011 extension/reroute, but worth reconciling against whatever source justifies the 129 km figure.
